A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HybridVLA. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLBench experiments, real-world single-arm and dual-arm evaluations, generalization tests, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and robot experiments and reports additional full-HybridVLA real-world results and revised ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same architectures, diffusion-before-autoregression token ordering, hybrid loss, training stages, four-step DDIM inference, KV cache, and confidence-gated ensemble with threshold 0.96. v3 expands the mechanism explanations and evaluates existing variants more broadly; it does not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The 35-dataset pretraining mixture, ten RLBench tasks, five Franka tasks, five AgileX tasks, and four generalization scenarios are retained. Appendix A and Table 6 preserve the dataset coverage. Additional model configurations evaluated on these tasks do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: External baseline membership remains unchanged. However, the denoising-step comparison removes Ex2, independently trained diffusion, and Ex5, without large-scale robotic pretraining: v1 Figure 3 compares three variants, whereas v3 Figure 4 shows only HybridVLA-dif. These comparators remain elsewhere in Table 3.

E3.justification: Core training budgets, demonstration counts, and 20-rollout evaluations remain unchanged. Local configuration changes include evaluating full HybridVLA in real-world experiments, replacing HybridVLA-dif with full HybridVLA in generalization tests, retaining robotic pretraining in the revised no-state Ex6 control, and extending the denoising sweep to additional step counts.

E4.justification: Component validation is substantially revised. Table 1 adds autoregressive evaluations of all four token layouts. Table 3 removes Ex7 and replaces the joint no-pretraining/no-state ablation with an isolated no-state control. The denoising analysis expands sampling-step coverage but removes comparative curves. Confidence-threshold tests, KV-cache analysis, and Appendix D's failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.1 newly reports three evaluations per model per task and adds plus/minus quantities labeled variance to Table 2; v1 reports point estimates without this information. This adds evaluation-variability reporting, but does not establish additional independent training runs or seed replication.

E6.justification: The main RLBench scores and speeds remain unchanged. v3 Table 5 retains HybridVLA-dif means of 0.80/0.66 and adds full-HybridVLA means of 0.83/0.71 for single-arm/dual-arm tasks. Generalization results now concern the full model. Table 3 replaces the 0.10 joint ablation with a differently configured 0.68 state-only ablation. New autoregressive token-layout scores and expanded denoising results further change the evidence; these are not same-setting improvements over the replaced configurations.

T1.justification: The action and feature definitions and diffusion/hybrid loss equations are retained. v3's discussion of shared gradients and token conditioning adds explanation, without new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain unified diffusion and autoregression, mutually reinforcing collaborative training, adaptive action ensembling, and strong manipulation and generalization performance. The abstract's added 14% and 19% margins restate differences already supported by v1's tables rather than changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains that autoregressive predictions cannot directly condition preceding diffusion tokens and attributes mutual improvement to joint optimization of the shared backbone. Its denoising discussion now emphasizes consistency with prior work rather than the earlier comparative pretraining argument. The inference-speed limitation and three failure categories remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies that the inference-speed comparison uses no action chunking and clarifies that autoregressive-only evaluation performs diffusion denoising before selecting autoregressive actions. These are additional disclosures, not established procedure changes. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, robot software details, and project-page information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the closest-prior-work context to unified multimodal and diffusion/autoregressive models, including Janus, Show-o, Monoformer, Diffusion Forcing, and Transfusion, explicitly distinguishing HybridVLA's robotics-specific contribution. It also adds dual-system VLA work such as GR00T N1, Agibot World, and Helix, while removing several earlier VLM/reasoning citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method and ablation narratives undergo substantial rewriting, particularly explanations of joint optimization and inference. The denoising discussion moves from Section 4.2 to Appendix B.2, and a broader-impact Appendix E is added. Much of Appendices A, C, and D remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned around comparison with previous architectures, Figure 2 revises the denoising illustration, and the denoising plot becomes an appendix bar chart. Tables gain rows or reorganized columns, and real-world qualitative panels are combined with Table 5. Retained appendix visualizations are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper by evaluating the full ensemble on real robots, adding simulation variability reporting, clarifying the mechanism, and acknowledging closely related unified models. These gains are tempered by removed ablation comparators and an incorrect Ex6-versus-Ex1 comparison in the state-embedding discussion. Overall, the evidence and explanation improve modestly while the underlying contribution remains unchanged.
